rulings.reason: Correct on the text. [0088] gives the ranges as those 'within which the mechanism is expected to operate with a seat ring (30) of that material and wall geometry'; [0091] 'The ranges correspond to the superelastic seat ring (30) with a convoluted wall (32)' and must be adapted for polymer, resilient-metal, other geometries, wiper ring (132) and larger bores; [0094], [0146] and [0161] repeat this. Claim 67 recites no material, claims 76-77 apply the claim 67 ranges to PEEK, and claim 16 on claim 8 has neither the convoluted wall nor the material. Best defence, [0006] (disclosure of a range is disclosure of every sub-range), does not answer it: it goes to sub-ranges, not to the material and wall to which [0088] ties them. The fix must also cover the combinations listed in F-28-4 (dismissed as its duplicate): claims 41-44 reached through claims 9, 24, 51-53 and 57, and claim 82, which recites no material or wall. The 'seat ring wall thickness' definition in [0028] (convoluted wall only) is part of this finding; see F-28-6.

Correct on the text. For the illustrated embodiment the purge gap is 'an annular radial clearance between the outer surface of the seat ring 30 and the core body bore 22' ([0018], [0040], [0053], [0102]), and 'In the illustrated embodiment the radial deflection is outward' ([0020]; [0054] 'radially outward, as described for the embodiment of FIG. 3'); FIG. 3 plan 'seat ring deflected radially outward, purge gap open'. [0103] states that such a gap 'opens where the bounding portion of the outer surface ... moves away from the core body bore', by inward or non-uniform movement, and [0110] likewise. An outer surface moving outward inside a rigid bore closes, not opens, that clearance. The wiper ring has the same contradiction ([0093], [0125], [0162], FIG. 10 plan: 'deflected outward ... opening a purge gap between the wiper ring's outer surface and the core body bore'). No passage reconciles it for the only built embodiment, and claim 29 read with claim 30, and claim 72, rest on it. The clearance drawn in the FIG. 1 closed state is dealt with under F-28-9. The rewrite must also cover the flutes (362) of [0110] and the FIG. 13B plan ('when the seat ring's outer surface moves inward'), raised in F-29-7.

Correct on the text. The poppet opens by moving 'towards the chamber side, lifting the sealing face (42) from the sealing edge (34)' ([0046]), so the sealing face lies on the chamber side of the sealing edge. The purge shoulder is 'on the chamber side of the sealing face' ([0038], [0052], [0112], claim 3), so it moves away from the seat ring in the opening direction. [0079] seats the ring at the end opposite the sealing edge, and [0116] calls the end remote from the sealing edge the 'chamber-side end', which would put the sealing edge on the supply side, the opposite of [0046]. No paragraph names the ring surface that the shoulder bears on. For the purge exit, [0036]/[0053] place the interference band at the internal shoulder, while [0056]/[0059] send the purge flow 'to the chamber side of the seat ring' by no stated route past that band. registry.md flag 3 records the FIG. 6 convention as 'a drafting assumption ... not a confirmed mechanism'. [0105]/claim 31 (a gap between the inner surface and the poppet 'on the chamber side of the sealing edge') cannot be placed either. Severity stays high for the claim set. Claims 3-4 may be unworkable as literally drafted ('chamber side of the sealing face'), so the inventor's layout must be checked against the claim 3 wording in the same fix. This ruling covers F-28-5, F-29-1 and F-29-2, dismissed as its duplicates.

Duplicates F-28-1: the same defect (ranges of [0089]-[0090] tied by [0088], [0091], [0094], [0146], [0161] to the superelastic convoluted seat ring but claimed with other materials, wall forms and formats), with the same two routes (confirm and add disclosure, or narrow). Its additional claim list (41-44 through claims 9, 24, 51-53 and 57; claim 82) is carried into the F-28-1 ruling, so nothing is lost.

Duplicates F-28-3, which is upheld on the same text ([0038], [0046], [0112], [0116], claim 3: the purge shoulder 'on the chamber side of the sealing face' moves away from the seat ring in the opening direction, and the contacted face is never stated). The F-28-3 ruling requires the inventor's layout to be checked against the claim 3 wording, which is this finding's specific remedy.

Duplicates F-28-1, whose attack states that 'seat ring wall thickness' is defined only for a convoluted wall yet claimed via claim 8, and whose action includes redefining it in [0028]. The premise is correct ([0028] 'radial thickness of the material forming the convoluted wall'; [0089] likewise; claim 16 depends on claim 8, not claim 11), and the fix is made under F-28-1.

Duplicates F-30-1: the same attack on [0009] ('consistent with the corresponding structures described in this specification and their equivalents') inviting 35 USC 112(f) treatment of the genus terms, with the same remedy. Upheld under F-30-1.

Correct on the package. figures.md cites internal material throughout ('11.md', '14.md', 'Gate 2', '01 Q1/Q2', DA-, CB-, E- and N-codes). It says the thermal variant is not drawn because 'the inventor states doubt about pursuing it', and that DA-7/23/24 are not drawn because they 'cannot be closed without new matter'. registry.md line 47 instructs a footnote on the FIG. 6 sheet calling the convention 'Assumption A2 in Prompt 20, not an asserted inventor fact'. The package has no list or brief description of the figures, so these texts are the only source for one. Any carry-over onto a sheet or into the list is an admission against the applicant. It is fixable in place and needs no disclosure.

Correct on the package. The FIG. 1 instruction (registry.md line 11) says the remainder of the seat ring's outer surface 'is drawn with a small clearance to the core body bore (22) even in the closed state', and the FIG. 6 instruction (line 47) labels that free region 'purge gap (60), radial clearance'. Claim 1, [0013], [0018] and [0040] require the purge gap closed in the closed and normal-open states. The description can be read consistently: [0036] says 'not in interference', which is not the same as a clearance, and [0110] has the outer surface lying on the lands. So the defect is in the drawing instructions, and correcting FIG. 1 and FIG. 6A to show contact at rest cures it. That correction must also make the word 'free of the core body bore' in [0053] and [0133] consistent. Medium is right.

Correct in part, and upheld on that part. For the third arrangement, [0105] says the inner clearance is 'closed, or is sufficiently small to carry no significant flow' in the closed and normal-open states. 'No significant flow' is a relative term with no criterion. The main passage is described only as 'the passage past the sealing face' ([0019], [0045]), so the text never shows how the main-passage route differs from a purge path running 'along the poppet stem (41)' through the ring bore, as claim 1 requires via claim 31. The best defence, the definitional separation in [0019] and [0102] (opened by lifting versus opened by deflection), states the separation but does not show it for this arrangement. The axial-position limb (a gap 'on the chamber side of the sealing edge') is covered by F-28-3.

Correct on the text. (a) Claim 47 (superelastic alloy) on claim 24 (integral flexure section, core body 'formed from a resilient polymer or from stainless steel of spring temper') is self-contradictory, and so are claims 48-50. (b) Claim 99 on claims 76-77 (PEEK seat ring) conflicts with claim 90 ('tube stock of a superelastic alloy') and [0150] (PEEK injection moulded). (c) Claim 24 on claims 8, 16 and 17 contradicts [0096] ('no separate seat ring (30)'). (d) Claim 34 on claim 29 contradicts [0110], where the flutes open when the outer surface 'moves away from the core body bore'. (e) Claim 29 on claim 6 conflicts with [0054] and [0114] (ovalising: outward at the lugs, inward between them). (f) Claim 23 'over-moulding of the core body' is disclosed only for 'a polymer core body' ([0134]). The range limb duplicates F-28-1. The proposed change to claim 10 (excluding claim 5) is not needed; see F-28-16. The fix is dependency pruning only, with no supported scope lost.

The premise is confirmed. registry.md flag 3 says the FIG. 6 interference-fit/purge-gap convention 'rests on a drafting assumption (Prompt 20, Assumption A2), not a confirmed mechanism', and line 47 calls it 'not an asserted inventor fact'. Yet [0036], [0053], [0103], [0133] and [0151] present the axial band as an embodiment, and claim 21 claims it. Whether the inventor conceived the axial-band retention is outside the package. It is resolved by the inventor's answer to 01 Q1/Q2: if confirmed, delete flag 3 and the footnote instruction (the footnote is also removed under F-28-8); if not, claim 21 and those passages come out as unconceived matter. It goes to counsel at medium severity.

Correct on the text. Claim 40 sets the over-travel threshold by ring stiffness with a single-rate spring. [0122] says the ring's loading 'follows a stress plateau after an initial elastic rise', and that for a polymer or non-transforming metal the threshold 'is less distinct'. So between first contact and the threshold, the ring is loaded by the deflecting formation. It is then not 'at rest' as [0010] defines it ('not deflected by the purge shoulder'), and the poppet has left the 'normal stroke' of [0012] (purge shoulder spaced from the ring). Claim 1 requires the ring 'in its at-rest form' at every pressure up to the threshold. No paragraph says the sub-threshold elastic loading leaves the purge gap closed or places it within the normal-open state. [0051] and [0050] do not answer it. Medium stands.

Upheld at low. The best defence is [0127], which defines the term ('a defined wiping edge ... being a sharp-cornered edge set by the cut profile of the seat ring (30) and preserved by limiting the extent of electropolishing'), so the 'no measurable boundary' limb largely fails. Claim 27, however, omits 'sharp-cornered' and extends the edge to any deflectable ring element, including moulded PEEK rings ([0150]: no electropolishing) and stamped wiper rings, for which 'set by the cut profile' has no referent; [0149] is likewise confined to laser-cut rings. The least change is to recite 'sharp-cornered' in claim 27 (basis [0127]). Extending the edge to moulded or stamped rings needs the inventor's statement.

Correct: [0160] ends 'both of the failure modes described in the background, leak-down and blockage', and the package has no background section. The failure modes are defined at [0024] ('Blockage') and [0029] ('Leak-down'). Re-point [0160] to those definitions or supply the section. Low.

The premise that the combination is excluded is false. [0113] says only that with a tapered purge shoulder the seat ring 'need not have an axial-to-radial conversion geometry', which contemplates one that does. [0084] says each conversion geometry 'may be used with any of the materials', and [0143] discloses each alternative deflecting formation in combination with the others unless an incompatibility is stated. [0144] states only the converse dependency (a plain wall is used with a tapered shoulder). A frustoconical flank bearing on a convoluted wall applies an axial component as well as a radial one. No pruning of claim 10 is needed.

Duplicates F-28-11, limb (e): claim 29 on claim 6 against [0054] and [0114]. It is fixed there by excluding claim 6 from claim 29's dependency, which avoids adding a definition that would itself be contestable.

Not an enablement defect. Claim 84 inherits claim 79's step of 'raising the pressure differential above an over-travel threshold', so it covers only compressed-gas use that reaches the threshold. [0058] states that 'the air purge occurs with any inflation device that raises the pressure differential ... above the over-travel threshold' and that the threshold 'is chosen to lie ... within the pressure differential that the intended inflation device produces'; [0090] says the same. On chilling, claim 84 is not limited to a superelastic ring. [0075] and [0171] offer resilient-metal or polymer rings whose recovery 'does not depend on a phase transformation', [0099] offers positively driven recovery, and [0100] states recovery on warming. Whether claim 84 earns its place commercially is a counsel choice, not a defect.

Upheld at low, on two items only. (1) Claim 20 with claims 52-53: the 'approximately 0.03 mm' interference is given only for the NiTi seat ring ([0036], [0132], [0151], [0156]), and for polymer [0076] says only that creep 'under a sustained interference fit' is to be checked. The specific value for PEEK is an intermediate generalisation. (2) Claim 26 through claim 9: [0093] and [0125] say the wiper ring wipes 'a surface of the poppet' and never the sealing face, which seats on the fixed seat. Fix by a confirming sentence if conceived, otherwise by excluding claims 52-53 from claim 20 and claim 9 from claim 26. The other items are answered by the text. Claim 1 with 9, and 18 via 9: [0014] ('carried by the valve core'), [0132] (retention 'against the internal shoulder (24) or an equivalent locating formation' for any deflectable ring element) and [0143]. Claim 59: [0005] ('carried by' includes indirect) with [0139]. Claim 63: [0138] and [0143]. Claim 102: [0152] ('a check of the press-in force, or of the press-in travel'), which is by nature performed during pressing.

Upheld at low, in part. [0043] says 'below the over-travel threshold' where claim 1 and [0013] say 'not exceeding' / 'does not exceed'; align [0043]. 'Towards its at-rest shape' in [0013], [0014] and [0071] versus claim 1 'to its at-rest form': the claim wording is supported by [0060] and [0098] ('returns ... to its at-rest form'), but the definitions should be aligned so they cannot be read as partial recovery. Rejected limbs: the numeral (30) in claim 58 is correct for the core-body variant of claim 59 ([0033]), and reference signs do not limit. The [0160] background reference duplicates F-28-15, and the figure-instruction and registry clean-up duplicates F-28-8 (registry.md line 161 does say description and claims 'do not exist yet'; refresh it).

Duplicates the purge-exit limb of F-28-3, upheld on the same text: [0036] and [0053] (band at the internal shoulder), [0056] and [0059] (flow 'to the chamber side of the seat ring' with no stated route), and registry.md flag 3. The remedy of stating the band, the free portion and the exit route, and matching FIG. 3 and FIG. 6 to them, is the F-28-3 remedy.

Duplicates F-28-3, which is upheld on the ground that no paragraph names the ring surface the purge shoulder bears on ([0038] and [0052] 'bears on the seat ring'; [0116] only for the retainer variant).

Largely answered by the text. Claims 9, 18 and 19 recite no wiper-ring dimensions. Wall form is given in [0093] (plain, convoluted, other conversion geometries, or split) and [0084]. Retention follows from [0132] (any deflectable ring element held 'against the internal shoulder (24) or an equivalent locating formation'), [0134], and [0143] (each ring retention means disclosed with the wiper-ring embodiment). Material is given in [0075] and [0093] (spring-temper stainless steel). A skilled person can build a spring-steel wiper ring from this. The one real gap, that the wiper ring is never said to wipe the sealing face (claim 26 via claim 9), is upheld under F-28-19. The missing internal shoulder in the FIG. 10 plan is a drafting detail for the drawings, not a support defect.

The generalisation limb is answered. [0132] defines ring retention for 'the deflectable ring element', held 'against the internal shoulder (24) or an equivalent locating formation', and says 'Whichever ring retention is used, it leaves that portion free'. [0143] discloses 'the alternative ring retention means' in combination with each of the three principal embodiments, including the wiper ring (132). So claim 21 read on claim 9 has basis in [0133] with [0132] and [0143]. Claim 21 depends on claims 19-20 (interference fit) and does not extend the band to crimp or sleeve retention. The 'not an asserted inventor fact' limb duplicates F-28-12.

Correct as a prosecution risk on the text. Apart from [0145] (material, core body and convoluted wall), specific multi-feature combinations rest only on the blanket statement in [0143] that each alternative 'is disclosed in combination with each of the others'. An EPO examiner can refuse a fallback that selects one species from each of several lists (deflecting formation [0112]-[0116], wall [0081]-[0083], gap location [0103]-[0106], flow path [0109]-[0110], threshold [0119]-[0123], retention [0133]-[0134]) as an unsupported selection. A short section of preferred combinations modelled on [0145] costs little before filing. The fix pass must take the combinations from the claims as filed (the dependent-claim chains) and must not rely on the internal 'amendment paths' the finding cites, which are not in the package. Medium.

Upheld on the tier-linking limb. [0089] and [0090] give each parameter its own three-tier list ('in some embodiments'), and nothing states the intermediate or narrow tiers of different parameters together. [0006] covers sub-ranges of a single range, not combinations across lists, so a fallback pairing (for example) the intermediate inner-diameter and wall-thickness tiers of claims 16 and 67 is a two-list selection. Add sentences stating the tiers together. The limb tying the ranges to the NiTi convoluted ring duplicates F-28-1. Medium.

Duplicates F-28-2: the same contradiction between the outward deflection of the illustrated embodiment ([0020], [0053], [0054]) and the outer-surface gap and flutes that open only by movement away from the bore ([0103], [0110]). The F-28-2 ruling requires the rewrite to cover the flutes (362) and the FIG. 13B plan.

Duplicates F-28-9: the same FIG. 1 instruction (registry.md line 11, 'small clearance ... even in the closed state') against claim 1 and [0040], with the same remedy (draw contact at rest, or state what closes the clearance).

The premise is correct. [0077] and [0124] say the snap-back wipe 'carries no speed or force qualifier', and [0158] says the audible snap 'is not a measurement'. So no amendment to recovery speed, force or the snap has basis. Whether any recovery time or force was measured is inventor knowledge not in the package. It is resolved by the inventor saying whether such data exist; if not, the distinction over closing-stroke wipers rests on the ring being the seat itself (claims 8 and 26) and on the material (claim 47), both of which have basis. Low.

Answered by the text. [0092] states for the one-piece form, without a material qualifier, that 'the shape recovery of the seat ring (30) moves it across the sealing face (42) or an adjacent surface of the poppet (40)'. [0035], [0076] and [0161] give the PEEK seat ring 'the same convoluted wall (32) and sealing edge (34)' as Example 1. [0063] and [0124] confirm that the polymer's recovery movement 'is nonetheless a snap-back wipe'. A skilled reader derives the same wiped surface for the PEEK one-piece ring. The wiper-ring case is upheld under F-28-19.

Correct on the text. [0009] calls these terms combinations of 'a generic structural term with a statement of function' and gives each the meaning 'any structure capable of performing the recited function, consistent with the corresponding structures described in this specification and their equivalents', which tracks the 35 USC 112(f) formula. That invites construction limited to the described species and their equivalents. 'Threshold-setting arrangement' (claim 36) and 'deflecting formation' (claims 2 and 28) are the most exposed. Without 112(f), the 'any structure capable of' wording feeds a written-description attack on the genus. The structural definitions already exist at [0014], [0021] and [0022], so a redraft costs nothing. Severity is corrected to medium: the risk is US-only, no 'means' wording appears in any claim, and 'ring element' in claim 1 names structure, so claim 1 is unlikely to fall as drafted. This ruling covers F-28-7, dismissed as its duplicate.

Correct in part. Claims 1, 58 and 79 require that 'the poppet is in over-travel ... and produces a radial deflection' at 'a pressure differential exceeding the over-travel threshold'. [0123] (a separate purge actuator, 'the poppet (40) performing only its normal stroke') and [0066] (depressor-driven over-travel with 'the second spring stage (54) ... omitted', so no pressure threshold) are disclosed and fall outside every independent claim, which exposes them to the US disclosure-dedication rule. Claim 46 covers depression only 'additionally'. The other limbs are weaker. [0117] (a skirt on the poppet) is arguably still 'carried by' the core body or valve stem under the indirect meaning in [0005]. [0067] deflation purge is claimed in claim 88, and a valve built for deflation-only purge still has the structural threshold of claim 1. [0142] is a deliberately separate concept for counsel. Severity is corrected to medium: this is lost scope and design-around exposure, not a ground of rejection. Any reformulation of claim 1's trigger must be checked against the saved references #13, #14 and #16 (second path opened later in the stroke or above a threshold). This ruling covers F-30-4.

The premise is correct. [0159] and [0167] found the sealing edge and sealing face clean but 'Cured sealant film ... on the outer surface of the seat ring in the region of the purge gap (60)', which is the surface [0056] says the air purge crosses. [0165] and [0167] state that the data 'do not separate the cleaning action of the air purge from that of the snap-back wipe'. Claim 1 does not recite the wipe (claims 25 and 80 do). An examiner can therefore say the effect of the distinguishing purge gap is not shown and reformulate the problem as providing an alternative. Severity is corrected to medium. No saved reference (INDEX #1-#17) discloses a purge path opened by radial deflection of a ring element through poppet over-travel. The nearest (#13, #14, #16) open second paths by movement of separate members, so even the alternative problem does not lead to claim 1 without hindsight. The finding's claim that this is common general knowledge is unevidenced. The fix is an inventor explanation or any data in [0169], with claim 1 not narrowed, and must invent no mechanism. Read it with F-28-2: whether the illustrated gap opens at all is unresolved.

The [0051] limb has a false premise. [0051] keeps 'a normal-open state' with the threshold 'set close to the crack pressure' and 'the normal stroke ... short', which is still within claim 1 (threshold higher than the crack pressure), and with the second stage omitted it falls within claim 40. No independent claim without the normal-open state is needed for it. The [0123], [0117] and [0067] limbs duplicate F-30-2, upheld at medium.

Duplicates F-28-2: the same contradiction between outward deflection ([0020], [0053]) and the outer-surface gap opening only by movement away from the bore ([0103], [0110]), with the same remedy. The FIG. 1 and registry limbs are covered by F-28-9 and F-28-12.

Best defence: [0053] says the gap opens when deflection 'moves a surface of the seat ring away from the surface against which it bounds the purge gap', and [0054]/[0103] disclose inward and ovalising deflection. That saves claim 1, but not the illustrated embodiment. [0020] says 'In the illustrated embodiment the radial deflection is outward', and [0040]/[0053] place the gap 'between the outer surface of the seat ring (30) and the core body bore (22)'. An outer surface moving outward approaches the bore, so it cannot open that gap. [0103] itself says a gap at the outer surface opens by 'an inward movement of the bounding portion'. The same contradiction appears for the wiper ring in [0093] and [0162] ('deflect the wiper ring radially outward, opening the purge gap between the outer surface of the wiper ring and the core body bore') and in the FIG. 3 and FIG. 10 instructions. [0036]/[0053] confine the interference fit to a band at the internal shoulder (24), but no text explains how purge flow from the supply side ([0056], [0059]) passes that full-circumference band to reach the chamber side; the flutes and ports of [0109]-[0110] are alternatives, not the illustrated embodiment. Claims 29 and 30 read together (outward deflection, outer-surface gap) and claim 72 recite the contradicted combination. High is right: the only built embodiment is described with a mechanism that cannot work as written. The fix needs the actual P-1 to P-3 mechanism from the inventor.

Claim 67 recites a seat ring with a sealing edge, a convoluted wall, shape recovery and two dimensions, but no poppet, over-travel, threshold or purge gap. Claim 90 recites a manufacturing route for such a ring. The feature they share with claim 1 is a ring deflecting radially and recovering, which claim 1 does not even limit to a convoluted wall. A posteriori, that shared feature is weak: saved ref US 9,982,818 B2, claim 1, discloses an SMA sealing ring with a 'wave-like shape comprising at least one peak and at least one trough'. Best defence under R. 43(2)(a), interrelated products, fails because claim 67 is not specifically adapted to claim 1's purge-gap/over-travel features ([0141] ties the matched kit to those features, but claim 67 does not recite the kit). Lack of unity plus the R. 43(2) objection to three product independents (1, 58, 67) needs amendment or division in the EPO and GB and will draw a US restriction. Lead finding on unity; F-30-24 is a duplicate.

Duplicate of F-30-13, which raises the same US multiple-dependency defect (37 CFR 1.75(c); e.g. claim 14 'any one of claims 11 to 13', where claim 13 is itself multiple dependent) and the same excess-claim fees at the USPTO, EPO and UK IPO. The objection is correct and is carried under F-30-13 at medium: a US preliminary amendment cures it with no change of scope, so high overstates it.

Claims 48, 74 and 95 recite 'austenite finish temperature below 5 °C'. [0026] defines Af only conceptually ('the temperature above which the superelastic alloy ... is fully austenitic'), and [0072]/[0148] say it is 'specified' without naming a test method. Different recognised methods (calorimetric and bend-and-free-recovery) can give different values for the same material, so a 5 °C limit without a method is an unusual-parameter clarity objection at the EPO and an indefiniteness point in the US and GB. Nothing in the text answers it. The method actually used, or specified to the supplier, for the prototype rings is inventor or supplier information.

The legal point is sound: EPO/GB added-matter practice does not treat a generic combination statement such as [0143] ('disclosed in combination with each of the others') as a direct and unambiguous basis for a selection from several lists. Severity is corrected to low. The description already gives explicit, independently usable fallbacks for the likeliest amendments: three-tier nested ranges for every parameter ([0089]-[0090]); named combinations of the three principal embodiments ([0145]); stated incompatibilities ([0144]); and a claim ladder that itself provides basis. The finding names no amendment that would actually fail. The residual risk is confined to multi-list combinations, e.g. polymer ring plus slotted wall plus flutes plus detent.

Best defence: this is a mechanical art; [0071], [0084] and [0122] explain the mechanism for each material and geometry, and prophetic Examples 2 and 3 ([0161]-[0162]) give constructions. Claim 1's defining contribution, however, is the purge flow path, and the text undercuts it. [0159] reports cured film 'on the outer surface of the seat ring in the region of the purge gap'. [0167] says 'The data do not separate the cleaning action of the air purge from that of the snap-back wipe'. [0091] says only the NiTi worked example was built. An EPO examiner can therefore treat the air-purge effect as not shown across the scope and reformulate the problem as an alternative. A GB breadth-insufficiency argument across untested materials and geometries is credible, though weaker in this art. Medium is right. Data isolating the purge are outside the package. Lead finding for breadth and credibility of effect; F-30-22 is a duplicate, and F-32-10 carries the specific combination attack.
Duplicate: the claim 31 limb is F-32-11 (upheld) and the claim 46 limb is F-32-12 (rejected). See those rulings.

The claim set has 102 claims. Claim 10 ('any one of claims 1 to 9', where claim 9 is 'any one of claims 1 to 7'), claim 14 (via claim 13), claim 18, claim 61 and claims 89 and 99 are multiple dependent claims resting on other multiple dependent claims, contrary to 37 CFR 1.75(c); the USPTO objects to them and does not examine them. Claim fees apply above 15 claims (EPO) and above 25 (UK IPO), with US excess and multiple-dependency fees. Claims 1 (valve core) and 58 (inflation valve) are separate product independents. The R. 43(2)(a) interrelated-products exception is arguable for 1 and 58 (claim 61 links them, and claim 58 alone covers the coreless valve of [0138]), but an objection is likely. The 1/58/67 limb overlaps F-30-7, which carries claim 67. Medium is right: no scope need be lost. Lead finding for the claim structure and fees; F-30-8 is a duplicate.

Claim 25 already recites the structure ('moves across a surface of the poppet') and then adds a result, 'shears sealant film from that surface', on material that is not part of the claimed valve core. The EPO allows result-to-be-achieved features only where the invention cannot be defined otherwise, and here it can. The result is also inconsistent with the description. [0063] says a superelastic ring shears 'rather than riding over it', while [0077] and [0124] say the snap-back wipe 'carries no speed or force qualifier' and include a weaker polymer wipe. So whether a polymer ring meets 'shears' is uncertain, and no shearing was measured ([0158]: the snap 'is not a measurement ... of the extent of the snap-back wipe'). Claim 80 is a method on a chamber that holds sealant, so the result language is less objectionable there, but it has the same measurement problem. A kinematic recast loses no scope.

Upheld for the terms not ruled elsewhere; 'associated with' is ruled under F-30-19, 'about'/'nominally' under F-30-23 and 'shears sealant film' under F-30-14. (i) 'Closed' purge gap in claims 1, 58 and 79: [0105] allows the clearance to be 'closed, or ... sufficiently small to carry no significant flow', so 'closed' has no fixed meaning. This matters for prior art with a small standing clearance. (ii) 'At-rest form' in claim 1: [0010] defines 'at rest' by the purge shoulder, which claim 1 does not recite. It is readable as the undeflected form, but the definition should be restated. (iii) Claim 55 'hard low-adhesion coating': relative, with only examples in [0129]. (iv) Claim 64 'tyre set-up': [0025] defines it only as a volume. (v) Claim 79 'surfaces on which sealant film accumulates': identified only by result, though [0056] names the surfaces. (vi) Claim 95 'verified on sampled seat rings': no sampling or method is stated. Each can be reworded from existing text. Medium stands because item (i) sits in every independent claim. F-32-13 is a duplicate.
Duplicate: the missing sections and the dangling reference in [0160] are F-30-21 (upheld). The drafting-process content in the figure plan and the FIG. 6 footnote instruction are F-32-5 (upheld).

Correct on the text. [0088] says 'the numbers follow from' the relationships, but the four relationships it gives are qualitative inequalities, not a design relationship linking over-travel distance, convolution amplitude, wall thickness and strain. [0091] and [0156] admit that the over-travel distance and purge gap opening 'were not measured'. Severity is corrected to low. The worked example gives every dimension needed to build the tested ring (2.3 mm ID, 0.20 mm wall, 3.0 mm free length, 0.12 mm amplitude, 0.5 mm over-travel: [0089]-[0090], [0156]). [0049] gives over-travel stops that bound the load. Adjusting within the claimed ranges in this mechanical art is routine trial, so claims 13, 35 and 43 are exposed evidentially rather than falling.
